Hi Alicia —

Appreciate the MAP draft. I attached a prefilled Redwood MAP template with the baseline econ assumptions (redwood_map_template.xlsx). High level answers below — these are conservative starting assumptions we use for early procurement/mutual-action planning. We'll tighten them during the POC when we get real prompts and payload sizes.

Baseline econ assumptions (POC-friendly, conservative):
- Model profile: medium-context summarization (avg response length ~180 tokens).
- Tokens per request (end-to-end): request tokens ~70, response tokens ~180 => ~250 tokens per interaction.
- Calls per end-user (test profile): assume 3 interactions per active user per week for initial forecast.
- Cost bands (hosted): at 250 tokens/interaction, expect $0.008–$0.015 per interaction depending on model family and quantization. Use $0.012 as an early planning figure for the MAP.

Caching guidance:
- Good candidates for prefix caching: boilerplate triage prompts, EHR field mappings, templated system instructions.
- Conservative cache-hit assumption for planning: 15% prefix cache hit across requests without additional engineering work; can be 25–35% with client-side routing and template normalization.

Batching and latency (POC settings):
- Recommended dynamic batch size: 8–12 on A100-equivalent infra for mixed small/medium responses.
- Queueing budget: 50–100 ms per request to enable batching while keeping median latency low.
- Expected 99p latency uplift at these batching settings: +80–160 ms compared to no-batching. If 99p SLO is strict, we can set lower batch windows and accept higher cost.

Suggested MAP / eval timeline (dates relative to kickoff):
- Day 0: kickoff + data share (sample prompts, traffic profile).
- Days 1–3: baseline POC config, ingest sample prompts, run smoke tests for tokens/profile.
- Days 4–10: run controlled traffic tests (concurrency and 99p latency measures), validate caching hit assumptions.
- Days 11–14: quality evals (manual and automated), finalize econ numbers for procurement.

Immediate asks from your side to firm up numbers:
1) Sample prompt set (10–20 representative requests including system + user text).
2) Expected weekly active users for the POC window and any burst patterns.
3) Any compliance/retention constraints that would affect caching.

If that looks reasonable I'm available for a 30m sync this afternoon (2:30pm PT) or tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks for the thorough breakdown and the prefilled MAP. That level of detail helps procurement a lot. We reviewed the assumptions internally and procurement asked for the following small tweaks to the MAP before sign-off:

- Please include a low/med/high cost band row in the MAP spreadsheet (we'll accept your conservative $0.012 as "med" but need explicit low/high for risk modeling).
- Can you add an explicit note about whether caching will store any PHI-derived prefixes (HealthSync rules: no persistent caching of PHI without explicit consent). If caching is limited to non-PII prefixes, confirm that in the doc.
- Procurement requested a firm 2-week POC window in the MAP with the controlled traffic dates listed (we'll lock them once we get the low/med/high bands).

We attached our procurement checklist for reference (HealthSync_Procurement_Checklist.pdf).

Next steps: if you can update the template with low/med/high bands and the caching note by EOD Monday, we'll route this internally and confirm the kickoff date (target kickoff the following Tuesday).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the POC.
